title: Make a 'yet' list: things you cannot do — yet
description: A one-page list that turns 'I can't do this' into 'I can't do this yet', with the smallest next step written beside each item. A paper habit borrowed from growth-mindset research.
author: SparkKindly · AI-assisted

body.heading: Write the list honestly
paragraphs: Take a blank page and write down things you currently cannot do that you wish you could: ride a unicycle, hold a conversation in another language, bake bread, do ten press-ups. Beside each one, add the word 'yet' — out loud as you write it. The word is small; the sentence it makes is a different claim about the future.

Then, for each item, write the smallest possible next step: not 'learn Spanish' but 'learn how to say good morning and count to ten'. A yet list fails when the steps are heroic; it works when they are almost embarrassingly small.

body.heading: Review it monthly, cross things off loudly
paragraphs: Keep the list somewhere you will see it — a wall, a notebook's first page — and review it once a month. Move one small step onto your calendar. When an item graduates from cannot to can, cross it off in a colour you cannot miss and write the date beside it.
The crossed-off items are the list's real engine: written proof, in your own handwriting, that 'cannot' has expired before. On the next hard day, that evidence is worth more than any pep talk.

takeaway: A yet list turns 'I can't' into 'I can't yet': write each wished-for skill, add its smallest next step, review monthly, and cross off graduates in bright ink.
materials: A pen, plus a bright pen for crossing off
A wall spot or notebook first page to keep it visible
supervision: A self-directed activity; younger children make their list together with a parent or teacher.
safetyNotes: Keep the list encouraging — it is a private tool, never a scoreboard to compare with anyone else.
Choose steps that are safe and age-appropriate; ask an adult before steps involving tools, cooking or sport.
If a step keeps failing, make it smaller rather than abandoning the item.
